title: G2: 'pairing determines isotopy class' asserted without proof (backbone of enumeration)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Gap (G2): "pairing determines isotopy class" is used as the backbone of the enumeration but is stated without proof.**

In §bigon, immediately after Lemma `lem:bigon`, the solution asserts:

> "Two embedded arcs whose ends interleave cross exactly once, and a system of arcs with prescribed ends and exactly one crossing per interleaving pair is **unique up to isotopy**. Hence the isotopy class of an admissible matching is determined by its pairing of $\{1,\dots,10\}$ alone."

This bijection {isotopy classes of cells} $\leftrightarrow$ {admissible pairings} is the foundation of the entire enumeration (§enum), the attaching-map computation (§attach), and the $f$-vector $(5,6,3)$. Yet the uniqueness-up-to-isotopy claim is asserted with no proof or citation.

It is **true**: it is the standard fact that essential arcs on a disk with marked boundary points are determined up to ambient isotopy (rel boundary) by their endpoints, and that a bigon-free (minimal-position) arc system realizing a given chord pattern is unique up to isotopy. But it requires justification, e.g.:
- cite the change-of-coordinates / arc-uniqueness principle (Farb–Margalit, *A Primer on Mapping Class Groups*), or
- prove by induction on the number of arcs using innermost-disk isotopies to remove bigons and align endpoints.

Without this, the identification of $k$-cells with admissible pairings (and thus the claim that there are exactly $5,6,3$ cells in dimensions $0,1,2$) is not rigorously closed, even though the combinatorial counts themselves are correct.
